Key notes from the call (high level):
- Workload: low-latency interactive recommendations for checkout flows; traffic spikes during promotions.
- Current ask: keep P95 <= 120ms at peak bursts; sustain baseline traffic with smooth tail latency.

Questions for you (short answers will help speed things up):
1) Peak burst QPS observed (and how long do bursts typically last)?
2) Sustained QPS baseline?
3) Typical request size (tokens or avg characters)?
4) Any hard constraints on region or data residency?

Attachments: SLA-worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-dedicated-config-guide.pdf (doc)

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa and Karthik on the recommended pilot once we get the numbers.

Hi Tessa — thanks for the recap. Quick answers below so you can size things: 

- Peak burst: ~1,800 qps during 5–8 minute flash promos (we saw ~1,800 qps sustained for ~6 minutes last month).
- Sustained baseline: ~350 qps outside promo windows.
- Typical payload: ~220 tokens (recommendation prompt + minimal context).
- Region: must be US (prefer us-east-1), data storage minimal but we need encryption-at-rest and audit logs for vendor access.
- Procurement: ETA 6–8 weeks; cc'ing accounts@fastbuy.com for procurement contact (they’ll want a ballpark on committed vs on-demand pricing).

Two clarifications: is warm KV cache required to hit P95 targets? Also, can Redwood support automatic fallback to Hosted if Dedicated capacity is exhausted?

Appreciate a ballpark cost/option matrix and we can sync on next steps.

—Ellen

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 12:30:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Burst throughput vs tail latency — internal recommendation

Folks — reviewed Ellen’s numbers. Quick internal read:

Summary of constraints:
- Peak burst ~1.8k qps for ~6 minutes; baseline ~350 qps; payload ~220 tokens; P95 target <=120ms; region us-east required; encryption + audit logs.

Recommendation (short):
- Primary: Dedicated reserved pool sized for 2k p99/burst headroom with pre-warmed KV caches. This gives the best chance to hit sub-100ms P95 for the model families we typically recommend.
- Fallback: Configure automatic routing to Hosted API for overflow (policy-based) — expect 20–40ms extra latency vs Dedicated depending on model and queueing.
- Autoscale timeline: use fast-burst nodes + a small warm pool; warm pool prevents cold KV misses during the promo window.

Pilot proposal outline (we should offer this):
1) 6-week pilot: 2-week prep (provisioning + pre-warm), 2-week promo simulation, 2-week validation + ops docs.
2) Deliverables: latency/QPS report (per-route), cost/time spent, SLA worksheet filled, runbook for fallback.
3) Success criteria: sustained baseline P95 < 120ms and peak bursts meet P95 < 120ms at 95% of observed promos; no more than one failover event to Hosted during pilot.

Pricing notes: propose a reserved capacity rate + small per-token overage during bursts; we can provide a ballpark range once we pick model family (Llama 2.1x vs RedWood-xx will change GPU footprints).

Action items for Tessa: draft pilot proposal (scope + timeline + pricing bands) and include the attached pilot-proposal-FastBuy.docx. I’ll help size the pool and prepare the configuration guide.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
